You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team
**Status:** Privileged / buyer internal. The Seller's package is treated as the other side's draft, not as agreed positions.

## 1. Overall assessment

The Seller's cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not. Almost every liability, disclosure and completion-mechanic position departs from our playbook, and in several places the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts the Seller Update (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, title). We should not treat any item as settled, and nothing in this package triggers (or satisfies the preconditions for) our conditional fallbacks – **no Amelia Frost written authority has been given for the 20% cap or the 18‑month period**, so our response must hold the starting positions.

## 2. Departures from playbook and reasoning

### A. Liability regime

| Item | Seller position | Playbook | Reasoning / response |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cl 12.1 General cap** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m | 20% is our fallback, usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None exists. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal that 20% is available. |
| **Cl 12.2 De minimis** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our level; would strip out most individual operational claims. Counter at AUD 5,000. |
| **Cl 12.2 Basket** | AUD 250,000, excess-only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar (tipping) | Combined effect of de minimis + deductible basket is a hidden further cap of AUD 250,000 on top of the 20%. Counter at AUD 50,000 tipping basket. |
| **Cl 12.3 Claims period** | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval – not given. Counter at 24 months. |
| **Cl 12.3/13 "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Blanket override | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | This is the most dangerous drafting point in the package. It would sweep fundamental warranties, tax, IP, specific indemnities (Ironquay), payment covenants (Riverlark, bonuses) and completion obligations into the 20%/18‑month/basket regime by default. Reject outright; replace with an express statement that the general limitations apply **only** to General Warranty Claims and that each other category has its own regime. |
| **Fundamental / Title warranties** | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% of price, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept a 20% cap on getting what we paid for. If title fails, our loss is the whole price. Insist on 100% / 6 years / no thresholds / no knowledge qualifier. |
| **Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature"** | No carve-outs | Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance | Absent an express carve-out, the Seller could argue that even fraudulent misstatement is capped at AUD 4.8m and time-barred at 18 months. This is non-negotiable per playbook and no one on our side has authority to waive it. Add a fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out to each of 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 and Clause 12 generally, "to the maximum extent permitted by law". The non-reliance clause also needs a carve-out for the Warranties and the Disclosure Letter itself. |
| **Tax / IP warranties** | "Settled under the general regime" | OPEN; separate categories; no unlimited liability but no resolution | Not agreed. Tax and IP are open items with their own cap/period to be negotiated. Respond that these remain open and must not be folded into Clause 12 by the "all Claims" language. Do not concede unlimited liability either – simply reserve. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – general disclosure of entire data room (DD‑002 to DD‑012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records.**
Playbook: specific fair disclosure only; reject whole‑data‑room, public‑register or prudent‑search deemed disclosure.
Reasoning: general disclosure means every document in the room qualifies every warranty regardless of whether a reasonable buyer would have identified the issue. Combined with Cl 8.3 (below) it would make the warranties close to worthless. Require: (i) disclosure must be "fair, specific and with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter"; (ii) delete public‑register and Accounts general disclosure (or limit to specifically identified extracts attached to the letter); (iii) delete any "deemed disclosed" or "prudent search" language. Note [1.4] (no admission of liability/materiality/requirement) is standard but should not be allowed to undercut the specific indemnities or conditions.

**Cl 8.3 Buyer knowledge – no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records".**
Playbook: delete blanket buyer‑knowledge exclusions.
Reasoning: "discoverable" is a constructive‑knowledge standard – it is the deemed‑disclosure regime by another name, and extends to advisers. Delete entirely. If the Seller insists on any knowledge language, it must be limited to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals of matters *fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter*, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity. Correspondingly, any seller "awareness" qualifier in the Warranties must reference named seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry.

### C. Conditions and completion mechanics

**Cl 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen (~AUD 3.6m, ~30% FY26 revenue; consent cl 11.2 with conditions in 11.3).**
Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent".
Disclosure Letter [2] concedes: **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** as at 22 Sept 2026.
Playbook: effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.
Response: Condition precedent must be (a) unconditional written consent from Bluefen in agreed form, and (b) documentary evidence that each 11.3 condition has been satisfied (or irrevocably waived by Bluefen), both delivered before Completion. "Satisfied on delivery" of a bare consent letter is inadequate if 11.3 conditions remain outstanding – Bluefen could still terminate. Seller obligation should be "all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours" plus a specific obligation to procure, with buyer right to approve the consent form. Consider a price‑protection mechanism if consent is not obtained (retention/escrow or termination right), to be discussed with Amelia Frost.

**Cl 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m; change‑control cl 8.1; discharge cl 9.2).**
Seller: release "to be provided following Completion".
Disclosure Letter [3] concedes: **not repaid; no final discharge in the data room**.
Playbook: current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post‑completion release only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
Response: Reject post‑completion release. Require: (i) Riverlark payout letter dated to Completion; (ii) repayment directly from the Completion funds flow (price is debt‑free/cash‑free, so this is a price mechanic, not a seller concession); (iii) executed deeds of release/PPSR discharge of all security, including any security over the shares, delivered at Completion; (iv) Riverlark consent or waiver under cl 8.1 change‑control before Completion. If the Seller cannot deliver a release at Completion, the only acceptable alternative is Riverlark's irrevocable written undertaking to release on receipt of funds, and that requires Amelia Frost sign‑off.

**Funds flow – DD‑005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420,000).**
Seller: "a matter for the Seller", not itemised.
Disclosure Letter [5] concedes: not in the funds flow; silent on payroll tax, super and on‑costs.
Playbook: bonuses plus triggered on‑costs must be a specific line item or seller‑funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
Response: These are triggered by Completion and will be paid by the Company post‑Completion – i.e. by us – unless addressed. Require either (a) a specific deduction line in the funds flow for AUD 420,000 plus superannuation, payroll tax and any other on‑costs, or (b) express treatment as Debt/transaction expense in the completion accounts, or (c) a seller indemnity with retention. Ask the Seller to confirm the gross figure including on‑costs.

### D. Specific risk items

**Cl 11.1 – Ironquay IP (DD‑004 cl 7.3; DD‑010 shows AUD 180,000 open).**
Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate".
Playbook: broaden the indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
Reasoning: Title to SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until every SOW3 fee is cleared. The Seller's indemnity covers only the payment amount, not the consequences of not owning the IP (loss of use, re‑development cost, third‑party claims, customer impact). Response: (i) broaden the indemnity to all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have unencumbered rights to the Project Materials, uncapped by the general regime; (ii) preserve the cure route – make payment of outstanding SOW3 fees and delivery of a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay a Completion deliverable; (iii) request bank evidence of payment status rather than relying on DD‑010.

**Cl 4.6 / Sch 6 – Export/privacy incident (DD‑006; ~1,240 records).**
Seller: "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material".
Disclosure Letter [6]: investigation preliminary; no finding on access, scope or notification; no loss amount.
Playbook: preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or demand in either direction.
Response: Do not accept the Seller's materiality conclusion – there is no basis for it yet, nor for any contrary conclusion. Require: (i) pre‑Completion covenant to preserve all logs and evidence; (ii) completion of the investigation (or a defined interim report) with buyer access; (iii) ongoing updates and notification of any regulatory contact; (iv) a specific warranty that the disclosed facts are complete and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, sitting outside the general cap/basket/knowledge regime. No price adjustment is proposed at this stage.

**Supplier renewals – Sandbar (DD‑008/DD‑011; 3 x AUD 110,000).**
Seller: ordinary‑course operating costs.
Playbook: assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
Response: Neither accept the Seller's characterisation nor assert Debt treatment yet. Request: whether each renewal is committed/unavoidable, terminable, already accrued at the locked‑box/completion accounts date, and the timing of each. Treatment follows from those answers.

**Office lease (DD‑007) and Mossvale (DD‑009).** Lower priority. Confirm the lease notification obligation is notice‑only (no consent/termination trigger) and complete the notice pre‑ or at Completion. Confirm the Mossvale assignment restriction contains no change‑of‑control trigger; obtain a specific warranty to that effect.

### E. Title

Seller: title evidenced by the DD‑012 share register. Disclosure Letter [10] itself concedes this is only the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed verification.
Playbook: independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD‑012 is a supplied internal source, not proof.
Response: Require as Completion deliverables / pre‑signing DD: current ASIC company extract; constitution; share certificates (or confirmation none issued); PPSR search against the Company and Seller; Riverlark confirmation of any security over the shares and its release; Seller board resolutions and directors' authority to sell; evidence no options, convertible rights or pre‑emptive rights. Title warranties remain on the fundamental regime (100% / 6 years / no thresholds / no knowledge qualifier).

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Hold all starting positions** – 25% / AUD 6.0m cap; AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket; 24‑month general period. No fallback is available; no authority has been given.
2. **Reject the "all Claims" override** in Cl 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5. Limit general limitations expressly to General Warranty Claims.
3. **Insist on a separate Fundamental/Title regime** – 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside thresholds and knowledge qualifiers.
4. **Insert fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve‑outs** in every limitation, exclusive‑remedy and non‑reliance clause. Non‑waivable.
5. **Replace general disclosure with specific fair disclosure**; delete data‑room, public‑register and deemed‑disclosure language.
6. **Delete Cl 8.3** buyer‑knowledge exclusion; any residual qualifier must be actual knowledge of named persons, never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities; seller awareness tied to named persons after reasonable enquiry.
7. **Bluefen**: CP of effective written consent *and* evidence of 11.3 conditions satisfied before Completion; consider price protection with Amelia Frost.
8. **Riverlark**: payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, security releases and cl 8.1 consent at Completion. Post‑completion release only via irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
9. **Bonuses**: AUD 420,000 plus on‑costs as a specific funds‑flow line item or seller‑funded; obtain gross figure.
10. **Ironquay**: broaden indemnity beyond the SOW3 fee, outside the general regime; make payment and confirmatory assignment a Completion deliverable; verify the AUD 180,000 independently.
11. **DD‑006**: log preservation, investigation completion, updates, specific warranty and indemnity; no materiality conclusion either way.
12. **Sandbar**: request terminability/accrual/timing data before deciding treatment.
13. **Tax / IP**: record as OPEN with separate regimes to be negotiated; reject "settled under general regime".
14. **Title**: obtain independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, constitution, authorities, Riverlark security position) rather than relying on DD‑012.
15. **Use the Seller's own Disclosure Letter** ([2], [3], [5], [10]) in our response – it undercuts the Seller Update on Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses and title.

**Escalations to Amelia Frost (information only, no authority requested in this round):** Bluefen price‑protection mechanism; any Riverlark post‑completion release structure if the Seller cannot deliver releases at Completion.
=== END ADVICE ===
